title: Abeoforma whisleri Transient Transfection Protocol
author: Elena Casacuberta
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.zexf3fn

steps.title: Prepare cell culture and count cells
steps.instruction: Count Abeoforma whisleri cells from a culture that is 1 to 2 weeks old and grown in Marine Broth (MB) medium at 13 °C.

steps.title: Harvest cells for transfection
steps.instruction: Take 2 × 10⁵ cells per transfection condition and spin them down at 2000 g for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Wash cells with PBS
steps.instruction: Discard the medium, gently resuspend the cell pellet in sterile 1× PBS, spin again at 2000 g for 5 minutes, and discard the PBS.

steps.title: Prepare DNA electroporation mixture
steps.instruction: Resuspend the washed cell pellet in 20–25 µL of a mixture containing Buffer P3 (Lonza), 1–5 µg reporter plasmid, and 40 µg carrier DNA (empty vector such as pUC19).

steps.title: Electroporate cells using Nucleofector
steps.instruction: Transfer the 20–25 µL DNA mixture to a Lonza Nucleofector 16‑well strip (X Unit) and apply program CODE EN‑138.

steps.title: Add recovery medium and transfer
steps.instruction: Immediately after electroporation add 80 µL Marine Broth directly to each well. Then either transfer the well to a 6‑well plate containing 1 mL Marine Broth or wait 30 minutes before transferring.

steps.title: Incubate and screen transformants
steps.instruction: Incubate the cells and screen for transformants after 24 hours; the number of positive cells will continue to increase until 48 hours.

steps.title: Prepare high‑concentration DNA and controls
steps.instruction: Lyophilize DNA preparations and resuspend them to a concentration of at least 1.5 µg/µL. Use ultrapure carrier DNA (pUC19) at 20 µg/µL. Always include a well with no DNA as a negative control to distinguish autofluorescence from true transfection.
